text_fidelity: hashkivenu/he: the concatenated text matches the s12 block exactly. That covers all metegs, the punctuation '. ', '.', ':', the maqaf in כָּל־עַמּוֹ, and the encoding of defective Jerusalem as יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם (qamatz, meteg, CGJ, hiriq), which follows the scan-digitization rule. Both יְיָ tokens are j:divineName, and no other word is marked. The split before וּשְׁמוֹר keeps the single space inside the opening range, so no word boundary is lost or doubled.
hashkivenu/en: matches the s13 prayer block exactly, including the semicolon after 'behind us' and the final period. It contains no השכיבנו cue.

kaddish_chatzi/he: three paragraphs, one for each s12 prayer block, matching exactly. This includes the commas before וְאִמְרוּ, '.' after אָמֵן in paragraphs 1 and 2, ':' at the end, the maqafs in דִּי־בְרָא, דְכָל־בֵּית־יִשְׂרָאֵל and מִן־כָּל־בִּרְכָתָא, and the doubled לְעֵֽלָּא וּלְעֵֽלָּא with its metegs, kept as printed. The speaker label חזן and the instruction 'The Reader says half Kaddish.' are correctly left out of the prayer words.
kaddish_chatzi/en: three paragraphs matching s13 exactly, including 'say: Amen!' versus 'say Amen!' as printed and 'high, yea high'. The יתגדל cue is absent.
The draft modules record no unresolved uncertainty. Both s12 and s13 have empty uncertainty lists, and the approval record lists none unresolved.

canonical_scope: hashkivenu: the div corresp is the whole canonical prayer. Inside it, prayer-part milestones mark /opening (הַשְׁכִּיבֵֽנוּ … וְרַחוּם אָֽתָּה) and then /hapores_sukkat_shalom (וּשְׁמוֹר … יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם:), and an unattributed terminator closes the range. Under URN-scope rule 2, /opening ends at the next prayer-part milestone and the variant root ends at the terminator, so neither range overreaches. Both extents match day one exactly: there, /opening covers the same words and the hapores_sukkat_shalom div starts at וּשְׁמוֹר and ends at Jerusalem. The day-two modules add no URN.
Both languages put the same URNs at semantically matching points ('Guard our going out' ↔ וּשְׁמוֹר), so the aligner gets a two-row join.
kaddish/chatzi: the div holds the whole prayer, with yitgaddal, yehe_shemeh and yitbarakh reused, one milestone per paragraph and a final terminator. This matches the day-one part structure.
No complete Biblical verse is quoted, so leaving out any bible identity is correct.
language_markup: The Hebrew publication keeps root xml:lang='he', and each Kaddish paragraph carries xml:lang='arc'. This matches the day-one precedent (paragraph-level xml:lang='arc'). The English Kaddish and both Hashkivenu witnesses have no paragraph xml:lang. The text_qa paragraph_languages values agree.
code: draft_prayers.py:119-120 sets XML+'lang' on each newly created paragraph only when the witness has a truthy text_language. Root language and English witnesses are unaffected. The change is minimal and scoped as described.
The new test (test_marmorstein_day_two_excerpts.py:97-105) checks root 'he' and ['arc','arc'] on two paragraphs, using invented data.
non_blocking_observations: Day one also carries the sub-identity hashkivenu/hapores_sukkat_shalom/text inside its hapores div, in both languages. Day two has only the root. This is a reasonable trade-off: a deeper prayer-part milestone at the same point would end the root's milestone scope early. The consequence is that anything referring to …/hapores_sukkat_shalom/text with day-two priority will not find a day-two witness. The spine/expansion review should confirm it transcludes the root (or the whole hashkivenu), not /text.

text_language is used only on the 'parts' path. A verse or range witness that carries it would have it silently ignored. It also applies one language to every paragraph of a witness. Both are fine for the current recipe; consider rejecting it on unsupported paths if it is reused.

Day one prints וְנֶחֱמָתָא (hataf segol) and day two's approved reading has וְנֶחְמָתָא (sheva). The encoding follows the approved day-two reading, which is correct, since precedent does not override the scan. I mention it only so nobody 'harmonizes' the two later.

Not copying day one's aseret-ymei-tshuva gate is acceptable for these draft text modules, because the doubled le'ela is preserved as printed. The required selection audit is still open and is not approved here.
